newsitem.title: USA: United Parcel to announce new European services.
newsitem.headline: United Parcel to announce new European services.

text.p: Betting heavily on upgraded technology and its global expansion plans to maintain its lead in the package delivery business, United Parcel Service said it expects to announce new services in Europe Wednesday.

UPS Chairman and Chief Executive officer Kent "Oz" Nelson, speaking before a group of journalists Tuesday, said he would not provide details of the plan. "All I will say about it is that we will announce new services that will affect movement between countries," he said.
Stressing the importance of global growth, Nelson said "You can't be in this business in the 21st century without a global presence."
Also crucial to the company's strategy is maintaining cutting-edge technology.

"Last year for the first time we spent more on computers than we did on trucks," he said. "In today's lightning fast and complex business world, distribution and logistics are increasingly becoming strategic elements that are addressed in the boardroom...not just the shipping room."

Nelson said that over the past five years the company has spent well over $3 billion on technology infrastructure. Asked to compare UPS to competitor Federal Express , Nelson said, "Federal Express has taken a different tack, they want to be a large air freight business. The air freight business is a very up and down business. We want to be a (package and letter delivery) business."

Citing in part a weak international non-express air freight market, Federal Express Monday reported first quarter earnings fell to $1.08 per share from $1.33 a share in the same period a year earlier on revenues of $2.69 billion.
UPS is privately held and does not disclose quarterly earnings. According to company filings UPS' total revenue has swelled to $21.05 billion last year from $8.62 billion in 1986.

Nelson said UPS would be utilizing "a number of 727s that don't fly much" to fly cruise ship passengers to their destinations. "Cruise lines have a huge need to move people on weekends, they have trouble getting reliable carriers." He said, adding that the company doesn't have plans to become a full-fledged consumer airline.
